newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Briton killed in Hungary was on charity trip.
newsitem.headline: Briton killed in Hungary was on charity trip.

text.p: A British man clubbed to death in his caravan in Hungary on Tuesday on his way to Romania was on a charity mission, the British embassy in Budapest said on Wednesday.
"It seems they were in the middle of a four-week charity trip," embassy spokeswoman Katie Ransome told Reuters, adding that they were not acting for any particular organisation.
Michael Trevor Pollard, 63, was killed and his wife Jo-Valerie, 55, was seriously wounded when bandits attacked their broken-down caravan outside the north-eastern Hungarian town of Nyiregyhaza.
Three men were later arrested as suspects, police said.
The couple parked late at night near a bus stop after their car, pulling the trailer, broke down.
Police said the attackers first posed as policemen and approached the couple to demand fines of 2,000 forints ($10) each for parking illegally, which the couple paid.
They then returned to beat the couple and rob them, police said.
Jo-Valerie Pollard awoke from a coma and stumbled to the road where a passing bread delivery van driver spotted her and drove her to hospital, police said.
Ransome said Pollard, who is being treated in Nyiregyhaza hospital, had chest injuries and a broken jaw and would undergo an operation for her facial injuries on Thursday.
Police declined to release the names of the suspects but said two of them were 22 years old and one was 18.
The couple, who have three children aged 25, 21 and 18, were based in Yorkshire and had done several trips to Romania on behalf of a number of charities based in the county, Ransome said.
